A Slack app in your workspace whose client the Gateway holds, so apps can post to approved channels and match people by email.

**Used by:** [OpenCRM](/docs/apps/crm) for team agents that post to Slack (optional).

## Connect accounts

Each person connects their own Slack account once, in the Gateway, and every app that asks for it uses that connection. Apps never see the tokens. [How connecting works](/docs/connect-oauth)

- **Make the OAuth app here:** [api.slack.com](https://api.slack.com/apps)
- **Settings:** `SLACK_CLIENT_ID`, `SLACK_CLIENT_SECRET`
- **Built in:** nothing to add, only the client to set

### Redirect URI

Register this at the provider:

```text
https://<your gateway>/connect/slack/callback
```

`<your gateway>` is your Gateway's address, like `apps.example.com`.

An app that runs the sign-in itself lists its own callbacks under `redirectPaths` in its manifest entry; register those too, as `https://<app>.<your gateway><path>`. `pnpm everyapp provider show slack` prints every one.

### Make the OAuth app

1. Open [api.slack.com/apps](https://api.slack.com/apps) and select **Create New App**. **From a manifest** is quickest: your coding agent can write one from the app's scopes.
2. Pick the workspace. Under **OAuth & Permissions**, add the redirect URI above as a redirect URL, and the bot scopes the apps you run need.
3. Under **Basic Information → App Credentials**, copy the **Client ID** and **Client Secret**.

### Set it on your Gateway

From your EveryApp folder:

```bash
pnpm everyapp secret set SLACK_CLIENT_ID SLACK_CLIENT_SECRET
```

Each value goes in at a hidden prompt. Or, as an owner or admin, paste the client in **Manage workspace → Providers → Add OAuth provider**.

### Scope sets

Apps ask for named sets, never raw scopes, and the Gateway holds each app to the sets it declared.

| Set | Allows | Provider scopes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `channels.read` | Channels (read-only) | `channels:read`, `groups:read` |
| `users.read` | Members (read-only) | `users:read` |
| `users.email` | Members' email addresses (read-only) | `users:read.email` |
| `messages.write` | Messages (post as the app) | `chat:write`, `chat:write.public`, `chat:write.customize` |
| `channels.join` | Channels (join public ones) | `channels:join` |
| `channels.manage` | Channels (create, manage and invite to; open DMs) | `channels:manage`, `groups:write`, `channels:write.invites`, `groups:write.invites`, `im:write` |
| `files.write` | Files (upload) | `files:write` |
| `user-channels.manage` | Channels (as the installing person: read, manage, invite to) | `channels:read`, `channels:write`, `groups:read`, `groups:write` |

### Use it in an app

```ts
capabilities: {
  slack: { access: "read", scopes: ["channels.read"], why: "What the app does with it." },
},
```

### Check it worked

- `pnpm everyapp provider show slack` shows the client as set, and the redirect URI.
- Open the account menu → **Connected accounts** → **Connect Slack**. You land back in the Gateway, connected.
- `pnpm everyapp provider connections` lists who has connected.
